name: Syrian Arab Republic
tags: Israeli occupation of the Golan buffer

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 185,180 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 183,630 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Includes the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights as in the World Bank figure.

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 25,620,427). Grade B and a wide range: refugee returns since Dec 2024 (UNHCR ~1 million+) and no census since 2004.

activePersonnel.note: Syrian Armed Forces infobox: ~180,000-182,000 active after the SDF integrated on 25 Aug 2026 (citing ACLED, 27 Aug 2026; link marked dead). Low 100,000 reflects how many integrated units answer to Damascus in practice.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Conscription abolished (CIA Factbook 2025); no organised reserve. High allows for demobilised fighters and tribal/Druze/Alawite local forces that could be called up.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 181,000 minus infantry P roles (150,000). Covers the residual air force, navy, logistics and staff; mostly undefined after the 2025-26 reorganisation.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy: Syrian civil-war factions jointly fielded ~400,000-500,000 fighters of ~21 million (~2%); new volunteer state army, so 1-5%.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2022. GDP 82,342,766,164 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD rebased x 0.8005) / population 25,620,427 = 3,214 2011 int$. Range +/-25%. Last World Bank value is 2022; GDP since then is very uncertain (sanctions lifted 2025, reconstruction), hence +/-25%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2022. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 102,864,167,601 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 82,342,766,164 2011 int$. Range +/-25% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Last World Bank value is 2022; GDP since then is very uncertain (sanctions lifted 2025, reconstruction), hence +/-25%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. No SIPRI series since 2010 (4.06% then, World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS); post-transition budget not published.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2022: industry incl. construction (and hydrocarbons) 11.9% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-7% for oil-price swings. asOf 2022, wartime economy; very uncertain.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.03 -> 0.73. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/SYR/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 16.30% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.59 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.53-0.69). Mid 1 - 0.163/0.59 = 0.73. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.53 = 0.6. High: s 0.69 = 0.76. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 59% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Wheat output collapsed by drought (2025) and war; WFP food aid ongoing.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 12,825,612 x share of males aged 15-19 11.799% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 302,657. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

roadKm.note: asOf 2006: 68,157 km (61,514 paved incl. 1,103 km expressways). War damage since 2011 not quantified, hence low.

railKm.note: asOf 2010: 2,139 route-km (World Bank IS.RRS.TOTL.KM); much track out of service since the war (low, educated).

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 3 ports, 1 large + 1 medium = 2 (Latakia, Tartus); Baniyas oil terminal.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: not in the list of flags over 1,000,000 GT, so under ~1.6 million DWT; mid is an educated guess.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Donkeys, mules, horses; not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Syria is not listed among the nine nuclear-armed states in the FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 table. Al-Kibar reactor destroyed by Israel in 2007.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: familiar terrain, urban strongholds, population support for the post-Assad state uneven (Alawite coast, Druze south, Kurdish north-east).

notes: Transitional snapshot: the Assad regime fell on 8 Dec 2024; the new Syrian Armed Forces were built from former HTS, SNA and other rebel factions, absorbed the SDF on 25 Aug 2026 (Syrian Armed Forces article), and Israel holds the Golan buffer zone and struck most heavy equipment, aircraft, ships and SAMs in Dec 2024. No order of battle has been published: every equipment count is an educated guess (grade D) with deliberately wide ranges. Population and area from World Bank (incl. the Golan); GDP last published 2022. Doctrine archetype-insurgent because the force is still organised and equipped as ex-rebel light infantry.
